source.request: Investigate loss of contact with an undercover operative at a remote Supply-mining operation.

briefing.playerText: An undercover operative working for an allied Haven has stopped communicating from a remote Supply-mining operation. The operative's transmitter code has been provided. Travel to the mining operation, determine what happened to the operative, and recover them if possible.

map.notes: Grid cells define geometry. Gameplay resolves at Stage level. No tactical grid movement.

overrides.text: Security personnel are watching the workers more closely than the perimeter.
Recent movement is concentrated between the main facility and interior work areas.
The operative's transmitter signal is weak but detectable west of the main hall.
Coughing is audible from the holding area.
Several patients show a similar symptom pattern.
The cases are consistent enough to warrant outbreak-style containment and investigation.
The known transmitter signal is strong and originates inside this area.
Readings indicate hazardous radiation around the processing equipment.
The processing system is operating with an unstable damaged power feed.
The extraction system uses technology beyond what is expected for this mining operation.
Guard spacing and response discipline are inconsistent with a professional security force.
The patrol pattern leaves predictable gaps near the overseer's office.
Security activity centers on McGuffin and the facility records.
The archive is actively deleting records.
The transmitter code confirms this is the missing operative.
The local test logs contain repeated field pulses and output anomalies. They have useful measurements, but no consistent explanation.
The device has separable rig connections. Safe isolation needs a verified account of the pulse cycle.
The characterized pulse and aligned output suggest a directed weapon role. Its operating limits still need controlled testing.

overrides.outcomeText: The supervisor gives you the code for the Security-to-Office door. Enter it without spending a Tool charge.
McGuffin gives you the terminal access code. Enter code unlocks the intact terminal without a Tool charge.
Unlock the terminal intact. Destruction is an alternative, not a follow-up step.
Destroy the locked terminal instead of hacking it. Leaves recoverable wreckage; does not erase the separate archive.
Destroy the locked terminal instead of hacking it. Leaves recoverable wreckage; does not erase the separate archive.
The code is accepted. The security terminal is unlocked and intact. No Tool charge spent.
The worker reveals a concealed entrance beside Holding. The hidden store is now accessible.
The worker reveals a hidden safe room behind the Overseer office. Its concealed door is now visible.
The code unlocks the office door. No Tool charge spent.

Compared the local logs with repeatable measurements: output diverges during the rig extraction cycle. The pulse behavior is characterized and a Research question is recorded. The device remains unidentified; its maker and full capabilities are unknown.
Isolated the rig connections and detached the same complete device safely. It is eligible for Receiving recovery, with its field findings preserved.

discoveries.question: How does the advanced mining technology alter or increase Supply extraction?
What produces the repeatable electromagnetic pulse, and why does output diverge during the rig extraction cycle?

deployment.notes: This benchmark mission JSON is fully finalized except for the actual player deployment. The simulator must bind the selected deployed Unit and Tool instances before runtime creation. Mission Reality and tuned encounter thresholds must not be regenerated when deployment is bound.

simulatorArtifact.note: Wave 3 prototype: Incidents, basic combat, authored escalation and objective execution.
assumptions: Movement costs 60 simulated seconds per Stage transition.
Redial at the Gate takes 180 simulated seconds; no dialing interference modeled in Wave 1.
Time advances on actions and explicit waits, not while choosing.
Staffing tool codes are provisional generic Service identifiers outside Technician aliases; no specialist Services inferred.
Tools reserve charges while work is active and spend them only on commit; cancelled work spends no charge.
Specializations unlock a second eligible kit slot but grant no unimplemented specialist power.
Patient assessment/stabilization are bounded field actions, not an outbreak cure.
Passive non-consuming observations require undamaged instruments but do not consume action charges.

Provisional combat: each party member carries a basic ranged weapon separate from the two Profession Tool slots; 100 health, 18 damage per 30-second round. Guards have 150 health and deal 5 damage. A lone guard lasts three rounds against four armed party members. Defeat leaves a downed person, not a death.
Combat requires explicit engagement; dormant guards remain a security threat. Disengagement preserves opponents and permits doorway retreat.
Patient 03 receives the same authored assessment/stabilization actions as the other patients. Holding and office guards receive explicit combat Incident records.

User-authorized provisional negotiation: Diplomat II can negotiate surrender without a Tool charge; Reynolds surrenders with his two guards, McGuffin surrenders individually. No faction rewards, hidden knowledge or automatic prisoner extraction.

User-authorized provisional terminal destruction: Technician I or Soldier I spends one Tool charge, disables power and leaves the entire terminal instance as recoverable WRECKAGE. No matter disappears and no separate resource yield is invented. Destroying the terminal does not erase or restore the separate evidence archive.
Campaign result bindings report actual state; faction rewards, address values and mission-lead payloads still require authored content.

Signal receiver is mission-issued party equipment, separate from Scout Tools and personal slots. It travels with the advancing party; local qualified Actors can use its SIGNAL_DIRECTION_FINDING Service. Passive observation is non-consuming.

User-restored SURRENDERED state distinguishes accepted surrender from combat incapacitation (DOWN). Soldier II intimidation uses a provisional demand-for-surrender outcome; Diplomat II negotiation handles surrender terms. Both apply only their explicitly authored participants. Restraint accepts DOWN or SURRENDERED.

User-requested interview utility: completing any authored interview prepares the team for this mission's surrender conversations, reducing negotiation/intimidation from 3 minutes to 1 without changing competency, equipment or target-state requirements.

User-requested recovery abstraction: discovered recoverable loot and secured people with known traversable Gate routes may be chosen at debrief without prior hauling. Unselected assets stay local; no carrying capacity is authored. Selected destinations await room admission.

Holding persuasion reveals two authored equipment crates containing the staffing-test rifles. Crate contents keep authored physical IDs and hidden Reality; revealing a crate grants no scientific Knowledge. Terminal hacking and destruction are alternative resolutions.

Source resolution for operative departure uses the existing Processing radiation source. Ordinary work is blocked by active hostiles; authored negotiation and intimidation remain available. Hidden rooms and dialogue rewards are authored simulator content.

nodes.speaker: guard-yard-01
nodes.text: Visitors check in with Reynolds inside.

responses.text: Continue on.
Busy shift?
Anything unusual happen here lately?
Who is responsible for Gate security?
Your checkpoint procedure is sloppy. Who authorized this?

nodes.speaker: guard-yard-01
nodes.text: Same as usual. Reynolds handles anyone who needs more than directions.

nodes.speaker: guard-yard-01
nodes.text: Nothing you need to worry about. Reynolds can answer questions.

nodes.speaker: guard-yard-01
nodes.text: Reynolds. Why?

nodes.speaker: guard-yard-01
nodes.text: You can take that up with Reynolds.

nodes.speaker: guard-yard-01
nodes.text: Heading out already?

responses.text: We're done here.
We need a quiet medical transfer. Keep this checkpoint clear.
Stand clear. We are taking responsibility for this transfer.
We will clear the checkpoint by force.

nodes.speaker: guard-yard-01
nodes.text: Hold on. Why is that worker leaving with you?

responses.text: Medical transfer. Reynolds can confirm it.
We'll wait.
We need a quiet medical transfer. Keep this checkpoint clear.
Stand clear. We are taking responsibility for this transfer.
We will clear the checkpoint by force.

nodes.speaker: worker-holding-01
nodes.text: I don't know what they're doing with the sick people. They keep telling us to stay out of the way.

responses.text: Where do they keep spare supplies?
That's all.

nodes.speaker: guard-holding-01
nodes.text: Help if you're here to help. Don't start opening things you weren't asked to open.

responses.text: Understood.
Why are these people being kept here?
Who authorized the restrictions?

nodes.speaker: operative-01
nodes.text: Keep your voice down. I can move once the patients are safe or the source is contained. If you clear the yard checkpoint first, I can slip out early.

responses.text: Stay put while we make a route to the Gate.

nodes.speaker: worker-processing-01
nodes.text: They've been pushing this equipment harder every week.

responses.text: Who told them to keep running it?

nodes.speaker: reynolds-01
nodes.text: Don't wander. Head straight to the overseer's office, and keep the visit brief.

responses.text: Understood.
Anything we should know before we go in?

nodes.speaker: reynolds-01
nodes.text: Finished with the overseer? Where are you heading now?

responses.text: We are following up on the medical situation. Please keep the hall clear.
We are checking the route back to the Gate. Keep your patrol out of our way.
Back the way we came.
Stand down, or we will force our way through.

nodes.speaker: mcguffin-01
nodes.text: Good. You're finally here. Did they get the contamination under control?

responses.text: Yes. It appears contained.
Contained, but the doctor isn't there anymore.
That's what I was told.
Medical wasn't part of my briefing.
We have not assessed the medical situation yet.

nodes.speaker: mcguffin-01
nodes.text: And Processing? Reynolds said the line was still unstable.

responses.text: The secondary fault is isolated. The line is stable for now.
They're still working it.
We still need to inspect Processing.

nodes.speaker: mcguffin-01
nodes.text: What did the lab make of the last test?

responses.text: The readings diverged during the extraction cycle.
I didn't get the full report.
We have not reviewed the lab evidence yet.

nodes.speaker: mcguffin-01
nodes.text: Anything else I need to know?

responses.text: The hidden weapon in storage is still secure.
Nothing outside my assignment.
No.

nodes.speaker: mcguffin-01
nodes.text: Fine. Get the report to me when it's ready.

nodes.speaker: mcguffin-01
nodes.text: Who exactly sent you?

responses.text: The same people who are going to be very unhappy if this operation stops producing.
You don't need to know.
Enough.

nodes.speaker: mcguffin-01
nodes.text: You're not supposed to be here.

nodes.speaker: guard-yard-01
nodes.text: What do you need from this checkpoint?

responses.text: We need a quiet medical transfer. Keep this checkpoint clear.
Stand clear. We are taking responsibility for this transfer.
We will clear the checkpoint by force.
Nothing yet.
